zoe (Finance): Quick procurement bulletin: three short updates affecting p-card use and vendor thresholds. Read if you buy tools or manage events.
zoe (Finance): A) Temporary card rule: when charging a team p-card for a vendor > $1,500 but < $2,500, you MUST file a short PO follow-up within 3 business days in Concur with project tag. This avoids miscoding at month-end.
zoe (Finance): B) Vendor threshold change: new vendors with estimated annual spend >= $12k now require a light Vendor Risk check. This replaces the old $10k threshold. For anything < $12k use fast-track. Link: https://confluence.redwood/procurement/thresholds
ben (Events): heads-up: conference booth rental is $2,200. That sits above the p-card comfort zone. Should we submit a PO now?
zoe (Finance): @ben submit a fast-track PO selecting "events" and attach the invoice. That will route through Sourcing. Expect ~48h review. If you need faster, mark "priority" and DM me.
nora (Eng): small Q: we occasionally get $1,600 one-off licences for OSS tools. Is that treated like micro-purchase or small PO?
zoe (Finance): @nora treat $1,600 as p-card eligible but remember the 3-day PO follow-up requirement. Also include the project code and a one-line justification.
procure-bot: Reminder: Micro-purchase policy -> https://confluence.redwood/procurement/playbook#micro-purchase
ben (Events): thanks, will file the fast-track now.
zoe (Finance): Final note: legacy vendor accounts will be reconciled to the new $12k threshold next month; procurement will notify owners of impacted vendors. We'll host a 15-min Q&A tomorrow at 10:00 to walk through the forms.
ben (Events): appreciated :thumbsup:
zoe (Finance): I'll post the Q&A invite in #calendar and drop a quick checklist in #general after the meeting. Ping me for urgent exceptions.
